learnables.predictableError: the teen is en- + -najst: 'enajst'; like 5+ it takes the genitive plural ('enajst evrov'). Don't confuse it with 'ena' (1).
hearing/saying it as 'dvajset' (20) — the exam's classic 12-vs-20-vs-21 trap; the teen has -najst, while twenty is the irregular 'dvajset' (the other tens are -deset).
confusing it with 'trideset' (30) — the -najst / -deset pair is the whole difference
dropping the -i- to 'štirnajst', and confusing it with 'štirideset' (40)
confusing it with 'petdeset' (50); also 'petnajst minut' — genitive plural after it
confusing it with 'šestdeset' (60) — beginners hear only the 'šest-'
swallowing the -e- to 'sedmnajst'; the full 'sedem-' stays: 'sedemnajst'
swallowing the -e- to 'osmnajst'; the full 'osem-' stays: 'osemnajst'
confusing it with 'devetdeset' (90)
confusing it with 'šestnajst' (16); the tens end in -deset
the -e- of 'sedem' is kept — 'sedemdeset', not 'sedmdeset'
the -e- of 'osem' is kept — 'osemdeset', not 'osmdeset'
spelt with both t and d, but said as one voiced stop — 'devet-deset' comes out [devéd-desét], the way 'petdeset' is [pedesét]; the confusable is 'devetnajst' (19).
the counted forms — 'en evro, dva evra, trije evri, pet evrov'; from five up it is the genitive plural 'evrov', never 'pet evro'
genitive plural from five up — 'petdeset centov', not 'petdeset cent'; in speech the price is often just 'pet petdeset' with no currency word at all
an ordinal is an adjective and must agree — 'prvo nadstropje' (neut.), 'prva vrsta' (fem.) — not the frozen masc. 'prvi'
reading 'drugi' as 'other' where a floor directory or a date means 'second' — context decides, and it still agrees ('drugo nadstropje')
soft stem — neuter is 'tretje' and feminine 'tretja' ('tretje nadstropje'), not 'tretjo'/'tretji' everywhere
confusing 'četrti' (fourth) with 'četrt' (a quarter of an hour) — and with 'četrtek' (Thursday)
reusing the cardinal — 'pet nadstropje' instead of the ordinal 'peto nadstropje'
in writing Slovene marks an ordinal with a full stop — '6. nadstropje' is read 'šesto nadstropje', not 'šest'
the -e- of 'sedem' drops in the ordinal — 'sedmi', not 'sedemi'
the -e- of 'osem' drops in the ordinal — 'osmi', not 'osemi'
after 'v' the ordinal goes locative — 'v devetem razredu', not 'v deveti razred'
a calendar date puts the ordinal in the genitive — 'desetega maja', not nominative 'deseti maj'
formed straight off 'enajst' — 'enajsti', not 'enajstni'
mixing it with the clock — twelve o'clock is 'ob dvanajstih', while 'dvanajsti' is the twelfth (floor, date, grade)
calling it 'prvo nadstropje' on the English model — in Slovenia the ground floor is 'pritličje' and 'prvo nadstropje' is one flight up; location is locative 'v pritličju'
'v prvem nadstropju' — locative after 'v', with the ordinal agreeing in the neuter; not 'v prvo nadstropje'
'v tretjem razredu' (locative) for which grade you are in; a university year is 'letnik', not 'razred'
'on Monday' is 'v ponedeljek' — 'v' + ACCUSATIVE; a masculine day looks unchanged because its accusative is identical to the nominative. Not 'na ponedeljek' on the English 'on' model.
the fleeting -e- drops when it declines — 'od torka do četrtka', not 'od toreka'
'v' + accusative — 'v sredo', not 'v sreda'; the feminine -o is where the case becomes visible.
confusing 'četrtek' (Thursday) with 'četrt' (a quarter of an hour); 'on Thursday' is 'v četrtek'
confusing 'petek' (Friday) with 'pet' (five); the genitive in a range is 'do petka'
'v' + accusative 'v soboto' for 'on Saturday'; genitive 'do sobote' in a range.
'v' + accusative 'v nedeljo'; and it is the LAST day of the Slovene week, listed after 'sobota', not the first.
'in January' is the bare genitive 'januarja' (or 'v januarju') — never 'v januar'
English-shaped 'februari'; it is 'februar', and 'in February' is 'februarja'
the fleeting -e- drops — the genitive is 'marca' ('marca 2026'), not 'mareca'
'in April' is 'aprila'; beginners add a preposition and say 'v april'
'in May' is 'maja' — the same form as the girl's name Maja, which throws learners off; it is still the plain genitive
confusing it by ear with 'julij' (July); genitive 'junija' loses nothing
confusing it by ear with 'junij' (June) — the one letter is the whole difference
spelt and said with a v — 'avgust', not the English-looking 'august'
the fleeting -e- drops — 'septembra' for 'in September', not 'septemberja'
the fleeting -e- drops — 'oktobra', not 'oktoberja'
the fleeting -e- drops — 'novembra', not 'novemberja'
the fleeting -e- drops — 'decembra', not 'decemberja'; and month names are lowercase in Slovene
'this week' is the bare 'ta teden' with no preposition; and the fleeting -e- drops in the plural — 'pet tednov', not 'pet tedenov'
'for a month' / 'in a month' is 'en mesec' / 'čez en mesec'; and 'mesec' also means moon — the month is meant only in a time phrase
the genitive plural is irregular 'let' — 'pet let', not 'pet letov'; dual is 'dve leti'
'over the weekend' is 'čez vikend' or 'za vikend' — not 'na vikend' on the English 'on' model
BOTH 'od' and 'do' take the genitive — 'od ponedeljka do petka', 'od osmih do štirih' — not nominative 'od ponedeljek do petek'
Slovene counts forward to the COMING hour, so 'pol sedmih' is 6:30, not 7:30; the hour goes genitive plural ('pol sedmih', 'pol desetih').
counting backwards like English — 'četrt na sedem' is 6:15 and 'tri četrt na sedem' is 6:45, both pointing at the COMING hour; in speech you'll also hear 'petnajst čez šest' and 'petnajst do sedmih'.
genitive plural from five up — 'pet minut', not 'pet minute'; the dual is 'dve minuti'
putting it after the time on the English 'five o'clock sharp' model — Slovene says 'točno ob petih', with 'točno' in front
a person is late with the verb — 'zamujam' — while 'zamuda' is the delay itself: 'Vlak ima deset minut zamude.' (genitive after the number).
leaving a bare pause between two clauses instead of joining them with 'in' — the speaking rubric listens for it; note that inside a number 'in' is written as one word ('enaindvajset')
'potem' sequences what comes next ('Najprej ..., potem ...'); it is not the cause word — that is 'ker' — nor the result word 'zato'.
putting it at the end of the clause like English 'though', or reaching for 'pa' — 'ampak' opens the contrasting clause after a comma: 'Rad bi kavo, ampak nimam denarja.'
swapping it with 'ker' — 'ker' gives the cause, 'zato' the result ('Dežuje, zato ostanem doma'); and it is not the question word 'zakaj'
the same word also opens a yes/no question; between two nouns it is plainly 'or' — 'Kavo ali čaj?', and both options take the same case.
agreeing 'to' with the noun ('Ta je knjiga', 'Ta je moja žena') — 'to' stays the invariable neuter, and two or more things take 'To so ___.'

learnables.gloss: In the picture there is / are ___.
learnables.predictableError: 'na slika' — after 'na' for a location it is the locative 'na sliki'; and the verb switches to 'so' for two or more ('Na sliki so trije ljudje.')

learnables.gloss: ___ is here / here's where ___ is (pointing something out)
learnables.predictableError: this is the LOCATIONAL 'here is' — pointing at where a thing stands ('Tukaj je banka.'). Handing something over is 'Izvolite', not 'Tukaj je'.
